messages:
infra-nia: heads up — ap-sg dedicated pool is saturating, admission controller started returning 429s for several committed tenants ~1978881234
oncall-bot: ALERT: dedicated-admit-queue-growth detected in ap-sg (rule: admission_rate > 200 r/s, window 1m)
infra-nia: seeing queue length jump from ~40 -> 900 in 2m, tail latency > 4s, CPU/GPU util at 98% on commit-asia-1 pool
sre-eli: can you paste the admission log lines and the top offending tenant IDs?
infra-nia: logs: ```[1978881236] AdmissionDenied tenant=acct-472 cap=reserved_pool_commit-asia-1 reason=capacity_exceeded policy=fairshare_v3
[1978881240] AdmissionDenied tenant=acct-901 cap=reserved_pool_commit-asia-1 reason=capacity_exceeded policy=fairshare_v3
[1978881243] AdmissionRetry queued=432 headroom=0.0```
cust-eng-maya: we've already got 2 customer tickets for timeouts, one is mid-sized ecomm customer hitting production peak
ops-luke: autoscaler reports no free nodes to add due to AZ quota limits, and bursting is disabled for this pool (commit discount restrictions)
pm-raj: what's blast radius? are hosted fallbacks configured for these tenants? if not, we should classify SEV and engage sales/engage.
ashley: product concern — if this persists through the afternoon we risk SLA credits for two committed customers. Need temporary mitigation ASAP.
sre-eli: hypothesis — recent scheduler change to fairshare_v3 introduced per-tenant weight drift causing small tenants to be starved under bursty arrivals. Rolling back to fairshare_v2 fixed similar issue in eu-west previously.
infra-nia: proposing two quick mitigations: 1) enable burst-capacity for pool commit-asia-1 (allows short-term overcommit up to 20%) 2) bump weight for top 5 committed tenants to reduce 429s while we triage
ops-luke: burst toggle requires infra approval for potential cost delta. cost estimate for 1h of 20% overcommit ~ $6k — ok to approve?
pm-raj: approve temporary burst for 1 hour while SRE triages. open SEV1 and notify customers.
sre-eli: running rollback of scheduler change to fairshare_v2 on a single AZ as canary — command: ```rictl patch scheduler commit-asia-1 --set policy=fairshare_v2 --az=ap-sg-1```
infra-nia: applying bump to tenant weights (minimal, per-prod-safe patch): ```rictl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: TenantWeightPatch
metadata:
  pool: commit-asia-1
spec:
  updates:
    - tenant: acct-472
      weight: 2.5
    - tenant: acct-901
      weight: 2.0
EOF```
cust-eng-maya: I'll draft customer messages and surface the tickets to account teams.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT_STARTED dedicated-ap-sg-saturation thread=1978881234 severity=sev1
sre-eli: monitoring: queue length down to 120 after weight bump + one AZ rollback, tail latency back ~700ms. still watching for 10m to confirm stability
ashley: please capture root-cause postmortem and include mitigation to auto-enable hosted-fallback for committed tenants when admission > threshold
pm-raj: noted. I'll create SEV channel and loop legal if SLA hit looks likely
infra-nia: will follow up with detailed playbook steps and cost impact. closing interim updates unless anything regresses.
